messages:
Marta: Quick sync — arguing w/ @Nikhil about control-plane egress fallback. If regional relays hit capacity, do we fallback to a global peering path or a best-effort shared NAT? Need operator contract: IP preservation, auditability, cost attribution. Thoughts? :thinking:
Nikhil: I'd prefer global peering only as a last resort. Main constraints: preserve source IP for customer logging, and attribute cost to tenant. Global peering can obscure CIDR mapping.
Anna: Agreed on last-resort. Proposal: tiered fallback
- primary: customer-local relay (no SNAT)
- secondary: regional relay (SNAT optional, preserve via XFF)
- tertiary: global peering (SNAT + annotated audit)
Rob: Problem with XFF is a lot of our infra can't trust header authenticity without mTLS between relays. If we rely on XFF we need attestation. Also global peering will break some customers' allowlists.
Samir: Two quick implementation notes:
1) Make fallback decisions policy-driven, not hard-coded. Operator should be able to set: `fallback_policy: ["local","region","global"]` and `preserve_ip: [true,false]` per customer.
2) Emit an immutable event when fallback happens: `egress.fallback.v1` with fields: customer_id, from, to, reason, timestamp, request_id. Helps billing and audits.
Marta: +1 on immutable event. We also need an SLA semantic: fallback must be annotated as "degraded" in Console (so app teams know latency/cost changed).
Nikhil: What about NAT exhaustion in global peering? We saw this in the staging incident last month. If global SNAT pool is exhausted, fallback should try region with aggressive muxing or queue.
infra-bot: incident-bot: FYI — staging incident 2025-11-12 (EGRESS-THROTTLE) caused ~5% of requests to jump to global peering for 13m. Root cause: regional relay OOM + missing backpressure. See https://intranet/ops/incidents/EGRESS-THROTTLE-20251112 :warning:
Anna: From an operator surface perspective we should expose:
- per-customer `fallback_policy` (editable via Console + API)
- a `fallback_history` feed (last 7d) with counts and example request_ids
- a `force_fallback_to` manual override for incident mitigation
Rob: Security: any manual override must be gated (SAML groups + audit log + 2-person approval for global peering switch).
Samir: Small config sketch:
```
egress:
  fallback_policy:
    - local
    - region
    - global
  preserve_ip: true
  fallback_events_topic: kafka://egress.fallback.v1
```
We can wire the events to Billing + Console.
Marta: Rolling this out: propose canary flag `cp-egress-fallback=v1` rolled to 5% tenants for 48h, with automatic rollback on >1% error delta or >20% latency p99 increase. Needs a playbook.
Nikhil: Also add a constraint on allowlist: if customer has strict allowlist, we should default `preserve_ip=true` and avoid global peering unless they opt-in.
Anna: Ops checklist for rollout:
- add feature flag + metric alerts
- ensure `egress.fallback.v1` ingestion path exists (schema validated)
- add Console UI for policy
- create RBAC for `force_fallback_to`
- run chaos test simulating regional relay OOM
Rob: +1. I'll draft a short RFC for the attestation header + RBAC model.
Marta: Great — can we capture action owners?
- RFC (attestation headers & RBAC): Rob
- Event schema + Kafka plumbing: Samir
- Console + API surface: Anna
- Canary plan & playbook: Nikhil
I'll follow up with a quick RFC PR targeting next week's arch sync. Thanks all :thumbsup:
